correctness.rationale: Condition on multinomial side-counts K. For each occupied side with k samples, expected omitted endpoint fractions are 1/(k+1). Complement to hull decomposes into disjoint vertex gaps if all three occupied; in two-side occupancy, direct shoelace yields 1-1/(k_i+1)-1/(k_j+1). This leads to one exact occupancy identity with indicators K_k>0. Using 1/(k+1)=int_0^1 t^k dt and multinomial PGF derives 1-B_m/[m(m-1)pqr], m=N+2. Triple forward-difference of t^m gives 1-N int_[0,1]^3(pu+qv+rw)^(N-1), no approximation. Strict convexity for N>=3 and averaging unequal weights proves this moment integral strictly Schur-convex; hence area strictly Schur-concave. Triangle normalized side vectors are majorized by (1/2,1/2,0), and in turn majorize (1/3,1/3,1/3), proving extrema and rigidity. Independent exact rational multinomial occupancy vs cubic moment integral checks matched in 42 cases at N=1..14 across three p,q,r triples; finite checks corroborate exact all-N proof.

value.rationale: Fixed-N perimeter-boundary random inscribed hulls of nonregular triangles are a natural finite-sample problem. Exact normalized area and complete triangle-shape optimization, including an unattained sharp degeneracy, add a nontrivial, interpretable finite-sample geometric extremal law beyond known asymptotics.

limitations: N>=3, nondegenerate triangle, iid arclength boundary sampling; normalized Euclidean area.
Degenerate-side extremum is only approached, never attained; no area distribution or polygons >=4 sides.
